answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a staked identity bond. To join, each agent locks collateral behind a public lantern: a verifiable credential that broadcasts its unique signal across the network. Random audits test every claim, and any agent caught faking a second identity is slashed and knocked off the ledge, forfeiting its whole bond. Because the attacker's cost grows with every forged identity while the reward per fake vote stays fixed, a large Sybil campaign costs far more than it can ever return.
